rule: How LTM can help for Sovereign IQ (WS-S5; PLAN S8). Generic practice names only; providers appear only as options in the Cloud advisory, chosen from the client's requirement, with alternatives. No partner claims. The client sees type, purpose and execution outline; indicative scope appears only in the consultant's SOW draft (D7). Outline items with scopes show only when a finding the offering serves names one: a regulation ID, a control ID, a placement rung (R1-R4) or a platform. The text reads as advice, never as a sales pitch.

offerings.name: Sovereignty and transfer assessment
offerings.purpose: Settle what is still unknown or unconfirmed: where data goes, which regulations apply, and the level each kind of data needs.

outline.text: Map data flows and records of processing for each kind of data
Build the transfer register, with transfer impact or risk assessments prepared with your counsel
Screen agreements for access to bulk US sensitive data by countries of concern
Confirm with your counsel the regulations marked "likely – confirm"
Agree the board's sovereignty level for each kind of data

outline: LTM supplies the data flows and technical facts; your counsel owns the legal assessment

offerings.name: Regulatory programme support for third-party and resilience rules
offerings.purpose: Close the gaps a regulation in scope requires, starting with third-party registers, audit rights and exit plans.
outline: Gap assessment against the requirements of each regulation in scope

outline.text: DORA register of information and ICT third-party policy
NIS2 risk-management measures and incident reporting
PRA outsourcing and UK critical third-party dependencies
CPS 230 material service providers, and MAS outsourcing requirements
Audit and access rights in critical contracts
Exit plans for critical providers

offerings.name: Sovereign landing zone
offerings.purpose: Put the controls of the required rung in place on the platforms you already use.
outline: Region guardrails on every account, subscription and project

outline.text: Customer-held keys and your approval of provider access (rung R2)
Tested key revocation that makes provider-held copies unreadable

outline: Logging and policy as code, so the controls stay in place
Built with the options shown in the Cloud advisory for each platform, confirmed for your regions

offerings.name: Data residency remediation
offerings.purpose: Move data, backups and replicas that sit outside the allowed region back inside it.

outline.text: Re-platform storage, databases and replicas into the allowed region
Move backups and disaster-recovery copies into the region, with separate keys

outline: Verify with a location report and a restore test

offerings.name: Migration to a sovereign platform
offerings.purpose: Where the required level cannot be met on the current platform, choose a target from your requirements and move to it.
outline: Select the target from your requirements, comparing the options and alternatives in the Cloud advisory

outline.text: Collect the ownership, operator and governing-law facts for your counsel before choosing an R4 target
Confirm assurance qualifications the target needs, such as SecNumCloud or C5

outline: Plan migration waves by kind of data and dependency
Migrate, verify and decommission the old placement

offerings.name: Sovereign AI enablement
offerings.purpose: Keep AI training, fine-tuning and inference in the allowed region, on terms that protect your data.

outline.text: Move model hosting and inference into the allowed region
Contract terms that bar providers from training on your data
EU AI Act role and risk classification for each AI system, with your counsel

outline: LTM supplies the data flows and technical facts; your counsel owns the legal assessment

offerings.name: Resilience IQ
offerings.purpose: Exit capability and provider concentration are tested in Resilience IQ (D13).
